measurement_slot: The resident ANE worker was cleared before measurement; every guarded child checked again before and after loading.

direct_mlpackage_cpu_and_ne.interpretation: Every load was slow because coremltools compiled the source package to a different temporary .mlmodelc path for every MLModel object.

stable_compiled_mlmodelc_cpu_and_ne.interpretation: The specialization is paid once for a stable compiled-model path and compute configuration, and the cache survives process exit.

once_or_every_time.answer: Core ML's specialization is a one-time cost only when the exact compiled .mlmodelc path and configuration are stable. The spike's direct .mlpackage load path creates a new temporary compiled path and therefore pays the slow path on every load, in the same process and in a fresh process.

cache.documented_scope: Apple documents an OS-managed specialized-asset cache linked to the full compiled .mlmodelc path and configuration; it is not process-local.

safe_invalidation_control_1024.method: Compile the unchanged package to a second app-owned versioned .mlmodelc path without touching private OS cache directories.

tooling_limits: fs_usage was available only as root and was not run with privilege escalation.
xcrun xctrace was unavailable in the installed command-line developer tools.
No private Core ML or ANE cache directory was deleted, and no cache location is claimed from filesystem guessing.

attributed: Package-to-.mlmodelc source compilation is separate and took 5.909 s at 8192.
579.688 s of the stable-path cold load was reported by Core ML inside MLModel loadContentsOfURL, not by Python wrapper overhead.
The 577.914 s difference between cold and cached framework loads belongs to Core ML's prepare-and-cache envelope.

CPU_AND_NE compute plans preferred all expensive operations on ANE, while the much faster 8192 .all load preferred them on GPU; this identifies ANE specialization as the scaling-sensitive path rather than source-package deserialization alone.
unattributed: Core ML exposes no public timing split inside prepare-and-cache for ANE compiler work versus weight transformation or layout.
RSS and system wired/available samples bound process and host pressure but cannot identify ANE-resident bytes or separate allocation from specialization.
Cached load time includes compiled-model deserialization and runtime allocation, but those components cannot be timed independently with the available APIs.
MLComputePlan is static anticipated-placement evidence, not a runtime dispatch trace.

sequence_1024.result: .all did not materially change load time or placement at 1024.

sequence_8192.result: .all avoided the long ANE-specialization path by moving every non-constant operation to GPU; it is not an ANE load-time improvement.

scaling.characterization: Parameter count is constant and package size grows only 16.8% from 1024 to 8192, so weights and raw package bytes do not explain a 20.0x load increase. Lowered operation count grows 6.0x and global attention tensor dimensions grow with sequence length. The non-smooth ladder and opaque compiler prevent a defensible single exponent, but the scaling is in graph/device specialization, not parameter count.

safety.limitation: Owned RSS and system wired memory are observations; they cannot guarantee ANE allocation is bounded or prevent workstation pressure.

tooling: coremltools MLModel and CompiledMLModel load timing
MLModel.load_duration_in_nano_seconds / Core ML proxy timing for MLModel loadContentsOfURL
MLComputePlan with cpuAndNeuralEngine and all configurations
run_stages.run_guarded with memory-pressure and timeout aborts
psutil process scans before and after every timed load

production_path_observation.stable_directory_behavior: A directory artifact is loaded in place, preserving a reusable full path.
production_path_observation.archive_behavior: A file artifact is unzipped under a new synapse-ane-UUID temporary directory for each worker load.
production_path_observation.implication: A packaged 8192 artifact must be materialized once at a stable versioned path before worker startup; a new UUID extraction path would intentionally miss the specialization cache.

campaign_target: Do not optimize model math first. Persist the compiled 8192 .mlmodelc under a stable versioned install path and reuse that exact path and CPU_AND_NE configuration across worker starts. This turns the ANE specialization into a one-time install or first-run cost. Then target the remaining first-specialization cost only if installation cannot absorb roughly 10-12 minutes. Do not use .all as an ANE fix because 8192 placement moves to GPU.
